# nonUndefined

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** `undefined`.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonUndefined() — Checks whether a value is **not** `undefined`. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.4.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonUndefined<T>(value: T | undefined): value is T;
```

`nonUndefined(value)` is the same test as `!isUndefined(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

The test is `typeof value === "undefined"`, which is safe for a variable that was never declared, unlike a bare comparison.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type             | Description         |
| :-------- | :--------------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| undefined` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not `undefined`; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonUndefined(null); // => true
nonUndefined(0); // => true
nonUndefined(""); // => true
nonUndefined(undefined); // => false
```
